r.정치 구도: A federation of seven emirates, founded in 1971 when British protection ended. The Federal Supreme Council, made up of the seven rulers, is the highest body and elects the president. By convention the ruler of Abu Dhabi serves as president and the ruler of Dubai as vice president and prime minister. Most of the oil lies under Abu Dhabi, so it pays for a large share of the federal budget and carries the most weight. Half of the 40 members of the Federal National Council are chosen by electoral colleges that the rulers select and the other half are appointed, and the council advises more than it legislates. There are no political parties, and close to nine in ten residents are foreigners, so the circle of people who take part in politics is very small.

t.why: Dubai is a crossroads for aviation and shipping between the Middle East, Europe and Asia, while Abu Dhabi runs on oil and sovereign wealth fund money. It established ties with Israel under the 2020 Abraham Accords and joined BRICS in 2024, choosing to do business with the United States, China, Russia and India alike. When the war between the United States, Israel and Iran broke out in February 2026, Iranian missiles and drones hit the country heavily, and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz cut its crude exports sharply. In May of that year it left OPEC, saying it wanted to raise production faster. Saudi Arabia next door is a longtime ally, but the two backed different forces in Yemen and clashed in public in late 2025, after which the UAE pulled out its remaining troops. It has also been accused of arming one side in Sudan's civil war, which the government denies.
t.rel: A federation of seven emirates. It established ties with Israel in 2020 and, as a finance and logistics hub, practices pragmatic diplomacy, doing business with the United States, China and Russia alike.
t.korea: The two countries established diplomatic relations in 1980. In 2009 a Korean consortium led by Korea Electric Power won the contract to build the Barakah nuclear power plant, South Korea's first export of a nuclear plant. All four reactors were in commercial operation by 2024 and supply about a quarter of the country's electricity. South Korea's Akh unit has been stationed there since 2011 to help train local special forces, and in 2022 the UAE signed a contract to buy the Korean-made Cheongung-II missile interceptor. A CEPA signed in 2024 took effect in May 2026, South Korea's first free trade agreement with an Arab country. The UAE is also one of South Korea's main suppliers of crude oil.
t.know: Dubai's Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building, was built by a Korean construction company.
etext: Most of the crude lies in Abu Dhabi and is produced by the state oil company ADNOC. It has kept adding capacity, and it left OPEC in 2026 so it could sell more without being held to a quota. A pipeline to the port of Fujairah lets some exports bypass the Strait of Hormuz, but not enough to carry all of them.

Dubai has little oil, so it built up ports, airports and free zones early. Jebel Ali is the largest container port in the Middle East, and Emirates grew into a major airline on passengers changing planes in Dubai. There is no personal income tax and foreigners can set up companies easily, which draws financial firms and the wealthy.

A sovereign wealth fund such as the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority or Mubadala puts oil money into stocks, property and technology companies around the world. Lately they have been betting heavily on AI data centers and chips. The Barakah nuclear plant and large solar farms are also investments for life after oil.

Citizens are only about one in ten residents, so the country relies on foreign workers from construction and services to the professions. When missiles and drones struck and sea lanes closed in the 2026 war, it showed how much the country's standing as a safe base is worth. Dubai property prices swing widely.
